prerequisite_edges.rationale: Make the broad value topic independently assessable by requiring the learner to distinguish how Six Sigma can create operational, customer, or financial value rather than only repeat the topic label.
Turn organizational-goal alignment into an assessable capability: given a stated goal and project outcome, determine whether the project materially supports that goal and explain the linkage.
Create an assessable distinction between an organizational driver and the metric used to observe progress, including explaining why a proposed metric is relevant to the driver.
Make Lean concepts assessable through classification of value, flow, and waste implications in a described process rather than recall of the label alone.
Represent value-stream mapping as an assessable interpretation capability: identify process-flow information conveyed by a map and explain what it indicates about the current process.
Make DfSS road-map knowledge assessable by requiring recognition of the purpose and sequencing role of a DfSS road map in a design-oriented improvement context.
Turn basic FMEA into an assessable analysis capability: identify a failure mode, its effect, and the reasoning needed to prioritize or respond to the risk in a bounded example.
Make the Design-FMEA versus Process-FMEA topic independently assessable by selecting the appropriate FMEA context for a described problem and applying the distinction consistently.
Value-stream-map interpretation depends on understanding the Lean value/flow/waste concepts the map is intended to expose; this is a capability dependency, not an inference from source ordering.

Applying the distinction between Design FMEA and Process FMEA requires the basic failure-mode/effect analysis concepts represented by I.C.2; the dependency is semantic rather than a source-order rule.

subskills.label: Explain Six Sigma value mechanisms
subskills.capability_statement: Given a bounded organizational scenario, distinguish plausible operational, customer, and financial value mechanisms of Six Sigma and explain the causal link without claiming observed business impact.

subskills.label: Evaluate goal-to-project alignment
subskills.capability_statement: Given an organizational goal and a candidate Six Sigma project outcome, determine whether the project supports the goal and state the evidence or metric linkage needed to justify the alignment.

subskills.label: Connect organizational drivers to metrics
subskills.capability_statement: Given an organizational driver and several candidate measures, identify which measure materially observes progress toward the driver and explain the relationship.

subskills.label: Classify Lean value, flow, and waste implications
subskills.capability_statement: Given a bounded process description, identify value-creating versus non-value-creating activity and explain how flow or waste concepts affect improvement reasoning.

subskills.label: Interpret a bounded value-stream map
subskills.capability_statement: Given a simplified value-stream map, identify the process-flow information it conveys and explain at least one process condition the map makes visible without inferring unavailable performance evidence.

subskills.label: Recognize the role of a DfSS road map
subskills.capability_statement: Given a design-oriented improvement scenario, explain what a DfSS road map contributes to sequencing and decision structure without asserting a specific proprietary road map not present in the frozen source evidence.

subskills.label: Analyze a basic failure mode and effect
subskills.capability_statement: Given a bounded design or process example, identify a failure mode and its effect and explain the risk-analysis reasoning needed before an improvement response is selected.

subskills.label: Select Design FMEA versus Process FMEA context
subskills.capability_statement: Given a bounded problem context, distinguish whether Design FMEA or Process FMEA is the appropriate analysis context and explain the basis for the selection.

unresolved_dependency_candidates.reason: Drivers and metrics may support goal/project alignment, but the preserved title-level evidence does not establish that I.A.3 is a hard prerequisite for I.A.2. Keep it unresolved until stronger pedagogical or source evidence is bound.
DfSS road-map knowledge and FMEA may be related in practice, but the frozen source index does not prove a hard prerequisite relation. Do not infer one from section adjacency.

population_rule: Domain I is provisional Learning-owner pedagogy, not ASQ-authored prerequisite structure. Preserve every source-bound identity unchanged; admit only semantic capability dependencies with explicit rationale; keep uncertain relations unresolved; keep canonical_admission_ready=false until all six domains and cross-domain dependencies close.
next_population_batch: Domain II (23 frozen source requirements), partitioned into bounded sub-batches so each derivation can be validated independently.
